emma: Heads up, canary traffic on prod-dedicated 03 is seeing OOMs ~10m after the rollout of #4621 (kernel-router refactor) :warning:
emma: Repro on local with the same config: sequence length 4096, 8 concurrent streams, batch_size target 32 — memory climbs and then OOMs on the KV allocator
rajesh: Ugh, saw spikes in the nightly perf job too. CI perf diff shows +18% P95 mem for longctx traces after merge 4621
luis: I ran perf on a smaller repro. Flamegraph points at kv_alloc_slowpath + a lot of waste in slab_rebalance. attaching snippet:
```
# perf top -g
kv_alloc_slowpath  45.2%  |-- slab_rebalance
kv_fetch_prefetch  12.8%  |-- kv_lookup
compaction_worker   9.6%  |-- compaction_scan
```
mira: pinging on whether the kernel-router now prefers the new `hetero-kernel-v2` path for seqlen>1024. That path changed the small-chunk allocation pattern in the cache in PR 4598
ben: quick bisect: reverted 4598 locally and memory profile goes back to baseline. 4598 touches the small-chunk allocator and changes eviction ranking to be time-first instead of size-first
dana: So sounds like interplay between kernel-router selection (4621) and the allocator heuristics (4598). Either one alone maybe OK, together they amplify fragmentation
ci-bot: nightly/perf: regression detected on branch main: mem_p95 +18% (compared to baseline 2 days ago). failing test: runtime/kv_mem_longctx
emma: Repro steps I used (local k8s dev node):
1) checkout main@3141590000
2) apply test config: `configs/longctx/seq4096.json`
3) ./scripts/run_inference_perf.sh --concurrency 8 --target-batch 32 --duration 600
4) watch `kubectl logs -f runtime-pod` for `OOM in kv-slab`

emma: Logs excerpt:
```
[2026-03-16T10:12:34Z] runtime: kv: slab alloc failed: requested=64KiB, free_small_chunks=12, free_large_chunks=0
[2026-03-16T10:12:35Z] runtime: kv: compaction started, scanned=2048 chunks
[2026-03-16T10:12:39Z] runtime: OOM: unable to satisfy allocation
```

rajesh: I kicked off a targeted bisect across the two PRs. Current results: revert 4598 -> no regression. revert 4621 -> partial improvement but still ~6% higher. Reverting both -> back to baseline
luis: I also inspected eviction score evolution. With 4598 the eviction_score decays faster for large prefixes which leads to more tiny leftover fragments. Screenshot: https://perflog.redwood/captures/314159-slab-evict.png
mira: Can we try a rollback candidate? We should either revert 4598 or gate hetero-kernel-v2 routing until allocator is fixed. Which is lower blast radius?
ben: Reverting 4598 is smaller (it only touches allocator heuristics); 4621 is broader. But 4598 fixes a small latency edge we wanted for short seqs. trade-off note: revert will regress short-seq latency ~3%
dana: Ops: holding canary progression on prod-dedicated 03. Notifying SRE for capacity to drain the nodes if OOMs hit customer traffic.

emma: Proposed short-term plan:
- revert 4598 in a hotfix -> rollback canary ASAP
- open follow-up: add unit tests for fragmentation (simulated small-chunk churn) + metric for fragmentation ratio
- longer-term: make kernel-router selection consider allocator state (prefer kernel that produces less fragmentation under high longctx load)

rajesh: I'll prepare the revert PR and include a perf job that runs seqlen=4096 scenario in CI gate

luis: Also adding a simple allocator snapshotting metric: `kv.slab.frag_ratio` and `kv.slab.avg_small_chunk_fill` to console dashboards

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: revert/patch-4598 -> env: canary-prod-03 by <@rajesh>. Awaiting approvals

mira: Quick checklist for revert: bisect output, perf graphs, logs, approval from eng-runtime leads, postmortem owner
ben: I'll draft the postmortem notes after revert lands

ci-bot: triggered job #perf-314159-bisect (bisecting main between refs: r4590..r4625). will report back

emma: If anyone wants to reproduce, I have a repro snapshot in /tmp/kv_frag_repro.tar.gz and a docker image `redwood/runtime:kvfrag-repro-314159`

dana: Thanks everyone. holding rollout and paging SRE if more OOMs show up. :handshake:
